After a two-year hiatus, Apple is developing a new iMac with the M6 chip and fresh colour options, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman. The new machine is expected to launch "before the end of the year."

The iMac's update cycle has never been particularly frequent — it skipped both the M2 and M5 chip generations, and still does not offer a larger display size, with Apple steering professional users toward the Mac Studio or a Mac mini paired with a Studio Display. Nevertheless, Apple is still preparing a new version of the iMac featuring the M6 chip.

Gurman says this update will bring "several new colours," though he offered no specifics. The 2024 M4 refresh made minor tweaks to the colour palette, but the seven colour options remained unchanged — only the shades were adjusted. The new iMac is also expected to go on sale before the end of the year:

That means this autumn could be a pretty significant season for the Mac. It could include a redesigned MacBook Pro with a touchscreen and tandem OLED, a new 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6, a new Mac Studio with the M5 Max and M5 Ultra (depending on supply), and a new iMac with the M6. Another possibility is a new Mac mini with the M6 and M5 Pro, though that is expected to arrive a little later.

Apple's M6 chip will be the first Mac chip built on the new 2nm process, but reportedly there will be no M6 Pro, M6 Max or M6 Ultra variants — Apple plans to accelerate the rollout of the M7 series.
